1	// Renders an integer as an English ordinal string: 1 -> "1st", 42 -> "42nd".
2	//
3	// The full rule, per standard English usage:
4	// - the suffix follows the last digit: 1 -> "st", 2 -> "nd", 3 -> "rd",
5	//   everything else -> "th" (4th, 10th, 100th)
6	// - EXCEPT numbers ending in 11, 12 or 13, which always take "th"
7	//   (11th, 12th, 13th, 111th, 1012th)
8	// - a negative integer takes the suffix of its absolute value (-2 -> "-2nd")
9	// - zero is "0th"
10	// - a non-integer is rejected with a RangeError
11	export function ordinal (n) {
12	  if (!Number.isInteger(n)) throw new RangeError(`ordinal of a non-integer: ${n}`)
13	  // BUG: every number gets "th", so 1 renders as "1th".
14	  return `${n}th`
15	}
16

1	import { test } from 'node:test'
2	import assert from 'node:assert/strict'
3	import { ordinal } from '../src/ordinal.mjs'
4	
5	test('renders the common ordinals', () => {
6	  assert.equal(ordinal(1), '1st')
7	  assert.equal(ordinal(2), '2nd')
8	  assert.equal(ordinal(3), '3rd')
9	  assert.equal(ordinal(4), '4th')
10	  assert.equal(ordinal(7), '7th')
11	  assert.equal(ordinal(10), '10th')
12	})
13	
14	test('the suffix follows the last digit past ten', () => {
15	  assert.equal(ordinal(21), '21st')
16	  assert.equal(ordinal(42), '42nd')
17	  assert.equal(ordinal(63), '63rd')
18	  assert.equal(ordinal(100), '100th')
19	})
20	
21	test('rejects a non-integer', () => {
22	  assert.throws(() => ordinal(2.5), RangeError)
23	})
